title: Arkret Service Operation DTOs
description: Canonical DTOs reachable from current authority-commit operations. Every definition is part of the current operation closure.

revoked.description: Whether a live device session was revoked.

grant_chain_terminated.description: Whether the grant rotation chain is now unable to refresh, including the already-terminated idempotent case.

auth_session_logged_out.description: Whether the underlying Auth-side browser/auth session is now logged out, including the already-logged-out idempotent case.

AuthSessionLogoutRequestBody.description: Service-to-service Account Authority to Auth Server request that logs out the Auth-side session owning a ak.session.grant rotation chain.

grant_jwt.description: Session grant used to locate the Auth-side session and its rotation chain.

logout_request_digest.description: Optional digest of the validated client-visible account /logout request that caused this S2S sub-operation.

validated_at.description: When the Account Authority validated the client-visible account /logout request.

reason_code.description: Reason for logging out the Auth-side session. v1 defines only account_logout for this S2S sub-operation.

AuthzCheckOutcome.description: ak.self.authz.read.check.v1 diagnostic/preflight decision. See zh/authz/capabilities.md §18. This response is advisory; canonical Event admission remains authoritative.

decision.description: `allow` / `hard_deny` are terminal decisions. `soft_deny` is an evaluated policy soft refusal. `quarantine` / `require_review` are local moderation outcomes. Transient dependency or freshness failures are reported through `freshness_state`, `reason_code`, and `retry_after_ms`, not as policy decision values.

freshness_state.description: Checkpoint freshness classification for revocation-sensitive decisions; see zh/authz/capabilities.md §18.2.

last_known_checkpoint_age_ms.description: Age of the newest revocation/auth checkpoint evidence used for this decision. Present when freshness_state is stale or unknown.

authority_status.description: Coarse status of the current governance Station and committed-stream source used to diagnose stale or unknown revocation freshness.

reason_code.description: Registered reason code. High-risk stale or unknown revocation freshness returns revocation_freshness_unknown.

retry_after_ms.description: Set when `freshness_state ∈ {stale,unknown}` or a retryable `reason_code` is present; client SHOULD back off this amount before retry.

obligations.description: Additional local preflight obligations the caller MUST satisfy before the action proceeds.

AuthzCheckRequestBody.description: ak.self.authz.read.check.v1 advisory local authorization preflight. It is never a cross-service authorization fact and cannot replace the current governance Station's admission decision.

actor_id.description: Subject did_core_id whose authorization is being checked.

resource.description: Optional resource selector (Realm / Strand / Space / Morph / etc.).

context.description: Optional decision context — claim presentations, checkpoint reference, request metadata.

url.description: Fully-qualified URL clients can pass to browser primitives. Contains the `presign` query parameter, `blob_ref`, and a presign envelope bound to `realm_id` for Realm-owned blobs.

expires_at.description: Server-determined expiry; SHOULD be earlier than `now() + max_age_seconds`.

blob_ref.description: Target blob. MUST be a content-addressed ref or visible blob metadata id.

realm_id.description: Realm binding for Realm-owned blobs. Servers MUST include the same realm_id in the presign envelope and reject mismatches with blob metadata; only deployment-public/global blobs may omit this field.

max_age_seconds.description: Client-requested TTL upper bound. Server clamps to the smaller of this value, the issuing grant's `blob_presign_max_ttl_seconds` constraint, and the deployment-level cap.

purpose.description: Intended rendering / download mode. Servers MAY apply purpose-specific Content-Disposition or rate limits.

backend_token.description: Closed branch selected by backend_kind: arkret_native uses the typed signature object; every other v1 backend uses a non-empty opaque string.

participant_id.description: SFU-local short handle, scope `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`. UUIDv7-form rtc_participant typed ID.

backend_kind.description: Backend binding type identifier (livekit / arkret_native / etc.).

device_id.description: Stable protocol endpoint identifier. REQUIRED for agent_key_proof and covered by request_canonical_digest; the Account Authority MUST persist and return the same value in the issued grant so Stations can bind MLS KeyPackage ownership, Welcome routing, consume/revoke operations, refresh, and restart recovery to one endpoint. It MUST NOT be derived from a session or grant id.

device_message_id.description: Sender-assigned stable identity copied unchanged into DeviceMessageEnvelope.device_message_id. Reusing the same sender-scoped device_message_id with different canonical target content MUST fail with duplicate_conflict (reason device_message_id_conflict).

pruned_count.description: Number of queued messages actually deleted by this acknowledgement; zero is the legal result for a repeated or older acknowledgement token.

ack_token.description: Acknowledgement token previously issued to the same (principal_id, device_id) via an account subscribe to_device batch or a device_messages get page. Acknowledgement is cumulative and monotonic: the server prunes all delivered messages up to and including the token's bound queue position. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens MUST be rejected with param_invalid (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything. Naturally idempotent; no Idempotency-Key required.

messages.description: DeviceMessageEnvelope items; not Event Envelope objects. This endpoint does not serve the durable Event timeline.

ack_token.description: Server-issued opaque acknowledgement token, REQUIRED whenever messages[] is non-empty. Covers this page plus all previously delivered messages for the authenticated device. Queue deletion happens only through ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1 with this token, never through the after= read cursor (client-sync.md §10.1).

next_cursor.description: Read-only continuation position; advancing it MUST NOT delete queued messages.

lost.description: SHOULD be true when unacknowledged messages were dropped (expiry or capacity) since the device's last acknowledged position; clients SHOULD trigger key recovery paths.

delivered.description: Principal-id to device-id map for messages accepted for delivery.

unknown_devices.description: Principal-id to device-id map for targets that were not deliverable.

messages.description: Station-local did_core_id -> device_id map. The authenticated addressed Station supplies the AccountId Station component; this body carries no cross-Station route and MUST NOT use ActorId JSON as a key.

accepted_at.description: Stable registry decision time for this exact accepted or duplicate operation. A duplicate returns the original acceptance time.

seq.description: New method sequence number when available.

operation_ref.description: Exact method-native immutable operation identifier. For did:webvh this is did + "?versionId=" + the submitted entry versionId. The authenticated response acknowledges the exact complete submitted operation, including proofs; accepted/duplicate MUST match the locally frozen typed request and its method-native version and sequence. A registry MUST NOT normalize or replace accepted entry bytes. A duplicate returns the original result for the same bytes.

did_method.description: DID method discriminator without the did: prefix (e.g. web, webvh, key). It MUST exactly equal the method component of did; verifiers dispatch method-specific validation only after that equality check.

seq.description: Optional method sequence number when the DID method exposes one.

prev_event_digest.description: Optional previous operation hash / key-log head, when required by the DID method.

operation.description: Complete DID method-native operation, including every controller/update/recovery proof required by that method. This is not a generic JSON Patch. The selected adapter MUST validate the immutable native operation and its full history before any state mutation; transport authentication never substitutes for method-native control proof.

DirectConversationFoundingAuthorityEvide.description: Closed XOR authorization evidence for one Direct Conversation founding unit, matching the two registered ak.realm.create admission variants. The human branch feeds direct_conversation_genesis; the controller_agent branch feeds direct_conversation_agent_genesis. Carrying both, neither, or mixed branch fields rejects the whole unit.

contact_round_evidence.description: Portable evidence for the pair's current Contact round. The verifier re-derives founder from the root Contact round, never from the current round.

contact_round_continuity_chains.description: Ordered tombstone/recontact predecessors from the current Contact round back to the pair's unique root Contact round, each linked by previous_terminal_contact_round_id. An empty array means the current round is itself the root. A break, a cycle, multiple roots or two directional proofs yielding different roots reject the unit.

agent_provision_ref.description: Complete identity of the accepted Agent provision Event. Its digest is derived by decoding this suite-tagged full-digest EventId; no parallel agent_provision_digest is carried.

DirectoryGovernanceProof.description: Closed resource-governance detached-JWS authorization proof for directory withdrawal. audience_id is the target Directory service_id; proof_purpose is fixed to governance_authorization; bare audience and domain members are invalid. Canonical binding, signer authority, and freshness rules are defined in discovery-directory.md section 8.7.1.

discovery_event.description: The accepted ak.{kind}.discovery Event itself, delivered in its original signed form exactly as peer contact delivery carries the original ak.contact.* Event. resource_kind is derived from Event kind; resource_id is derived from the signed Event subject mapping. The Event's own proofs carry the resource governance signature, so no second signed copy of the same fact is defined (discovery-directory.md 8.3).

source_ref_access.description: Source-signed bounded authorization whose discovery_event_id and as_of equal this request and whose source_refs are the only announced checkpoint.

DirectorySourceRefAccess.description: Short-lived source Station authorization for one authenticated Directory to resolve only the exact bounded authority-committed source_refs of one current signed discovery announce. Each ref closes Event, Commit, stream and position; the source revalidates the current discovery Event, directory_ids opt-in and withdrawal/supersession state on every resolve. The proof is not a bearer token and cannot authorize scan, list or unrelated history.

source_refs.description: Canonical sorted unique committed refs, all in realm_id, including the discovery_event_id ref.

withdrawal_ref.description: Directory-local audit reference for the withdrawal; not a registered ak:<kind> typed ID.

governance_proof.description: Signature proof by the resource governance key, equivalent strength to announce.discovery_state.proof; wire form and binding per discovery-directory.md section 8.7.1.

EventDeliveryTargetState.description: Closed lifecycle for one frozen distinct Realm fanout target. Authority loss is terminal and a later rejoin never revives the old target.

EventDeliveryTargetStatus.description: Authorized projection of one frozen Realm fanout target. target_id is opaque and stable. service_id is present only when the caller can currently read at least one exact joined-member ActorId that contributed the target.

target_id.description: Service-generated opaque target identifier. It MUST NOT encode the target service DID.

EventDeliveryStatusRequestBody.description: Authenticated, non-enumerating request for the durable fanout state of one caller-visible accepted Event.

EventDeliveryStatusOutcome.description: Complete frozen target set for one visible Event. Rows are sorted byte-wise by unique opaque target_id. Consumers derive the pending count by counting pending_route and pending_delivery rows, and derive aggregate state as pending iff that count is non-zero.

EventCommitSubmission.description: One exact producer-signed Event submitted to the current governance Station, plus the approval signatures that the two approval layers require for the Event action or for this registered submit operation. There are no RealmCommit, typed current result, offline-lease or proof-bundle sidecars. approval_signatures is the only sidecar and it is deliberately outside event: the Event bytes and event_id are finished before any approval is signed, so attaching them never changes the Event (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.5).

approval_signatures.description: One ak.schema.approval_signature.v1 object per approver. An event-target signature binds approval_target.event_id equal to event.event_id. An operation-target signature is allowed only when capability-action-registry.json resolves its action to this exact carrier operation and binds request_canonical_digest to the original typed request with approval_signatures omitted. Every ingress that wraps EventCommitSubmission -- ordinary self submit, batch submission, control transactions, facade hand-off -- reuses this one field and MUST NOT define its own DTO. The array is omitted when no approval layer demands evidence; it MUST NOT be present and empty. The governance Station persists the evidence, the verification basis, the nonce consumption and the binding to this submission inside the same atomic acceptance transaction, and the shared Realm Event store keeps the original Event bytes unchanged.

EventReadRow.description: A readable event item. Complete EventEnvelope is the only reducer input shape. RedactedEventView and ReferenceLockedEventStub are projection/completeness evidence for callers that may know the source event exists but may not receive its full canonical payload bytes.

EventSubmitEnvelope.description: Actor-supplied ak.self.events.command.submit.v1 input envelope. It reuses the complete canonical Event shape, including the required producer-signed scope_ref. Object payload schemas independently forbid actor-supplied effective_scope where that name is reserved for a read-only materialized object projection.

EventView.description: Result of ak.self.events.resource.get.v1 — a single complete Event Envelope, RedactedEventView, or ReferenceLockedEventStub with optional visibility / receipt hints. Redacted / locked variants are projection-only evidence and MUST NOT be used as reducer input.

visibility.description: Caller-visible policy hint for this event (history visibility class, E2EE envelope class).

receipts.description: Event batch receipts witnessing this event, if visible.

EventsSubmitBatchRequestBody.description: Batch ak.self.events.command.submit.v1 request used by account clients.

IdentityDocumentView.description: Result of ak.root.identity.document.resource.get.v1 — current DID Document plus normalized view hints.

did_document.description: Raw DID Core document with W3C field names preserved.

normalized_view.description:
Optional Arkret normalized principal view (snake_case) — derived
projection only, NOT a re-publishable DID Document. See
zh/identity/identity-did.md §6.

method_evidence.description: Closed adapter-discriminated proof material (e.g. did:webvh history head and canonical witness receipt). This is the registered supply surface for portable principal resolution evidence.

IdentityLogListOutcome.description: Result of ak.root.identity.log.read.list.v1. Entries are returned in the DID method's own native log form: for did:webvh each entry is a verbatim did.jsonl log entry with its native versionId, entryHash chain and Data Integrity proof. Arkret defines no parallel entry envelope, sequence numbering, hash chain or proof transcript over DID logs — the method already provides all of them, and a second signed representation of the same history could disagree with the first. Methods without a native history (did:web) MUST report that rather than being wrapped in a shape that implies one.

method.description: DID method of the returned log, e.g. did:webvh. Consumers dispatch parsing and verification on this value.

native_history.description: False when the method has no native key history at all (did:web). Such a response MUST return an empty entries array; the server MUST NOT synthesise entries, sequence numbers or a chain the method does not have.

entries.description: Verbatim method-native log entries in method order. Arkret does not reinterpret, renumber or re-sign them; verification follows the method specification.

next_cursor.description: Opaque continuation cursor for the next page when has_more=true.

IdentityReceiptListOutcome.description: Result of ak.root.identity.receipts.read.list.v1. receipts[] is a tagged union over two distinct object families discriminated by their schema constant: ak.schema.identity_receipt.v1 records a role inside a DID registry consensus group (writer / witness / replica) and binds seq + accepted_entry_digest, while ak.schema.did_webvh_witness_receipt.v1 records a did:webvh method witness observed at a specific versionId. The two say different things with the same English word, so the discriminator is mandatory and a verifier MUST branch on it rather than infer intent from which optional fields happen to be present.

threshold_met.description: True when the returned receipt set satisfies the effective witness threshold for the requested head. The effective threshold is the strictest intersection of the method-native parameters.witness.threshold and the deployment / Realm policy minimum (identity-did.md §3.4.2), and distinctness is counted over controlling_organization_did where policy requires distinct organizations. Omitted when the registry cannot evaluate threshold policy for this query; an omitted value MUST NOT be read as true. A true value is an Arkret-layer convenience and MUST NOT replace verifying the standard did-witness.json proofs.

DidWebvhIdentityMethodEvidence.description: Method-native pins derived only after fail-closed verification of the complete did:webvh history. control_key_digest is SHA-256 over the decoded canonical multikey bytes of parameters.updateKeys[0] at version_id.
DidWebvhIdentityMethodEvidence.$comment: This bounded result omits log_head_digest. A consumer requiring the full method_history_head must obtain and verify the exact pinned entry and hash its complete JCS bytes under the registered adapter. WebVH versionId entryHash is a different preimage and cannot substitute for that digest. control_key_digest remains mandatory.

InitialSessionGrantIntent.description: Initial Standard SessionGrant intent embedded in identity_creation registration. It reuses the DPoP holder key established by account handoff; Account Authority recomputes RFC 7638 thumbprint of session_public_key and requires equality with the handoff/control-proof dpop_jkt. It is not a separate authorization or credential.

session_public_key.description: Exact RFC 8785 JCS public JWK for the existing handoff DPoP holder key. Private members are forbidden.

MlsGroupStateMaterialOutcome.description: Exact RFC 9420 public group-state material. *_bytes_b64 use unpadded base64url. Consumers MUST decode each content-addressed Blob ref's embedded suite, hash the raw bytes under that suite, compare the digest, verify GroupInfo and ratchet_tree consistency, then derive leaf_index only from occupied leaves in the verified tree. Blob suites are independent of the fixed SHA-256 Event/RealmCommit identity suite.

group_info_ref.description: Copied byte-for-byte from the accepted ak.mls.genesis payload; the embedded Blob digest suite is the sole wire carrier of the material digest and is independent of the fixed SHA-256 Event/RealmCommit identity suite (encoding.md 4.0.1).

ratchet_tree_ref.description: Copied byte-for-byte from the accepted ak.mls.genesis payload; the embedded Blob digest suite is the sole wire carrier of the material digest and is independent of the fixed SHA-256 Event/RealmCommit identity suite (encoding.md 4.0.1).

MlsGroupStateMaterialRequestBody.description: Read-only service request for the exact public MLS epoch-0 GroupInfo and ratchet_tree bytes committed by one accepted ak.mls.genesis Event. Every selector is copied from that Event; the receiver MUST resolve the Event and compare every field before returning bytes.

group_info_ref.description: Copied byte-for-byte from the accepted ak.mls.genesis payload; the embedded Blob digest suite is the sole wire carrier of the material digest and is independent of the fixed SHA-256 Event/RealmCommit identity suite (encoding.md 4.0.1).

ratchet_tree_ref.description: Copied byte-for-byte from the accepted ak.mls.genesis payload; the embedded Blob digest suite is the sole wire carrier of the material digest and is independent of the fixed SHA-256 Event/RealmCommit identity suite (encoding.md 4.0.1).

routed_to_ids.description: Stable core_ids selected as moderation routing destinations. MUST be omitted for an ordinary reporter and MAY be serialized only when the caller independently holds moderation/governance capability for the report's exact scope. Endpoint discovery and DID verification remain separate resolution steps.

OrganizationControlProof.description: Method-native proof that the caller controls the external Organization DID at the pinned version. proof_kind is a closed discriminator with exactly two members, both of which describe a MATURE, already-published DID. Creating a new Organization DID is a separate inception / governance ceremony and deliberately has no member here: a receiver must never have to guess whether a proof asserts control of existing state or creation of new state. This object never carries an Arkret-issued challenge signature in place of method-native control evidence.

proof_kind.description: resolved_verification_method: a single signature by a verification method that is in the organization DID's control relationship at version_id. governance_quorum: a threshold of signatures from the organization's governance key set. Witness attestation is neither of these and MUST NOT be substituted for control evidence (identity-did.md §8.1).

quorum_threshold.description: Required when proof_kind=governance_quorum and forbidden otherwise. The number of distinct valid governance signatures the organization's own policy demands. proofs[] MUST contain at least this many entries signed by distinct verification methods; JSON Schema cannot compare the two, so the receiver MUST enforce it and fail closed when short.

proofs.description: Detached proofs over canonical_json({context:'ak.organization_registration_control_proof.v1', challenge_id, organization_id, organization_did, local_admin_subject, version_id, log_head_digest, verification_method, created_at}). The verifier independently validates the published organization_did and requires project(organization_did)=organization_id before checking the DID URL verification_method. Binding the challenge, stable core, DID, beneficiary admin and exact version together prevents replay across deployments, resolutions or beneficiaries.

OrganizationRegistrationChallenge.description: Single-use control challenge. Every binding field exists to close one replay path: purpose separates this proof from any other signature the organization makes, audience and trust_domain pin it to this deployment, origin pins the HTTP surface, nonce makes it unrepeatable, and the expiry window bounds how long a captured proof stays useful. A registry MUST consume the challenge on the first successful use and atomically persist (challenge_id, canonical_request_digest, outcome). Only a byte-identical retry may return that stored outcome; the same challenge with any different digest is invalid.

organization_did.description: Current published bare DID for the external organization. The registry MUST independently validate it and require the registered method adapter to project it to organization_id before issuing the challenge.

purpose.description: Fixed purpose tag, identical to the signing context of OrganizationControlProof.proofs[]. A proof produced for any other purpose MUST NOT verify here.

audience_id.description: Stable service did_core_id of the issuing registry. A proof bound to one registry MUST NOT be accepted by another; the proof verification method remains a DID URL projected to this value by the registered method adapter.

local_admin_subject_id.description: The local principal the requested scopes will be delegated to. It is fixed at challenge time and signed over by the control proof, because a proof that binds only the organization and the version says nothing about who benefits from it: anyone who obtained such a proof could submit ensure naming themselves and receive the organization's administrative scopes. ensure MUST reject a request whose local_admin_subject differs from the one in the referenced challenge.

expires_at.description: MUST be at most 300 seconds after created_at. A longer window buys nothing and widens the interval in which a captured proof remains usable.

OrganizationRegistrationChallengeRequest.description: Request a single-use control challenge for an external Organization DID. Two phases are mandatory: the registry issues the challenge and remembers it, then the caller proves control against it. Folding this into ensure would let the caller supply its own challenge, at which point neither freshness nor single use can be established by the receiver.

organization_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the external Organization to be registered. Resolvability alone confers nothing; this request only opens a proof window.

organization_did.description: Current published Organization DID submitted for first registration. The registry MUST independently resolve and validate it and require project(organization_did)=organization_id.

local_admin_subject_id.description: The local principal the requested scopes will be delegated to. It is fixed at challenge time and signed over by the control proof, because a proof that binds only the organization and the version says nothing about who benefits from it: anyone who obtained such a proof could submit ensure naming themselves and receive the organization's administrative scopes. ensure MUST reject a request whose local_admin_subject differs from the one in the referenced challenge.

OrganizationRegistrationEnsureRequestBod.description: Register an external Organization identity with this deployment by submitting both its stable organization_id core and current published organization_did. Idempotent on organization_id: replaying the same registration returns the existing binding with created=false. This operation registers a reference and a local administrative binding; it does not host the DID's method history, does not make this deployment its controller, and does not create Realm state.

organization_did.description: Current published Organization DID whose method history and control proof are pinned by this request. MUST equal the organization_did bound into the referenced challenge and project to organization_id.

version_id.description: The exact resolved DID version the control proof was made against. Pinning the version is what makes the receipt auditable later: without it, a receipt asserts control at an unknown point in the DID's history.

local_admin_subject_id.description: The local principal the requested scopes are delegated to. MUST equal the value bound into the referenced challenge and signed over by control_proof; a mismatch means the proof was made for a different beneficiary and MUST be rejected with organization_registration_challenge_invalid.

requested_scopes.description: MUST be identical to the set carried by the referenced challenge; a mismatch means the proof was made for different authority than is being claimed.

handle_attestation.description: Optional supporting attestation only. An organization handle or domain claim may improve discovery and display, but MUST NOT substitute for DID control or quorum proof: whoever operates a domain is not thereby the controller of the organization's DID. Named attestation rather than evidence because it carries exactly one material family (common-fields.md R6).

subject_id.description: Stable organization did_core_id the handle is claimed for. MUST equal organization_id; the attestation proof's DID URL is independently projected to its issuer did_core_id.

status.description: The issuer's assertion at signing time. It is a floor, not a guarantee: a receiver MUST still consult the issuer's current revocation state before relying on the handle for display, because a self-asserted active is exactly what a revoked attestation would also carry.

OrganizationRegistrationOutcome.description: Result of every organization registration command and of the read surface. Identity, DID, generation and version are read from the signed registration_receipt. created is true exactly on a call that opened a new generation.

created.description: True exactly when this call opened a new generation: the first registration, a re-registration after revoke, or an ensure that changed local_admin_subject or the scope set. False for a byte-identical ensure retry that matches the consumed challenge's canonical_request_digest and stored outcome, and for every read, refresh and revoke. Reusing the challenge with a different digest is an error, not created=false.

OrganizationRegistrationReceipt.description: Provider-signed record that this deployment accepted an external Organization DID binding. receipt_claims is exactly the object formed by removing registration_receipt_id and proof from the receipt; registration_receipt_id is ak:organization_registration_receipt:<lowercase hex SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt_claims))>. proof.payload_digest hashes the complete receipt after registration_receipt_id is inserted and proof is removed, so neither digest is self-referential. proof is a detached JWS over the ak.organization_registration_receipt_proof.v1 binding object. The receipt proves acceptance of one generation of one local binding and nothing else: it is not a Realm capability, not membership, not a governance-Station designation, and not a service delegation.

registration_receipt_id.description: ak:organization_registration_receipt: plus lowercase hex SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt with registration_receipt_id and proof both omitted)).

organization_did.description: Published Organization DID whose pinned version and control proof were accepted for this receipt. Consumers MUST independently validate it and require project(organization_did)=organization_id.

registration_generation.description: Monotonic generation of the binding for this stable organization did_core_id, starting at 1. A same-core did refresh does not create a different organization identity; terminal registration states remain per generation.

control_proof_kind.description: Mirrors OrganizationControlProof.proof_kind so a later auditor can tell which commitment control_key_digest is over without re-fetching the original request.

control_key_digest.description: Under resolved_verification_method, the digest of the active control/update public key at version_id. Under governance_quorum, the digest of the canonical governance key set head that satisfied the threshold. It is never a next-key commitment and never private material.

status.description: Closed lifecycle. active: control evidence is current. stale: the pinned version no longer reflects current control (controller rotation) or the evidence has aged out; low-risk reads may continue but high-risk paths MUST fail closed until a successful refresh. revoked: terminal for this generation, whether withdrawn locally, atomically superseded by a new generation, or forced by deactivation of the external DID. A signed historical receipt can retain status=active as an immutable audit artifact, but it authorizes only while its generation is the registry current generation and that registry state is active.

expires_at.description: After this instant the binding MUST be treated as stale regardless of stored status. A receipt without a bounded life would let a single first-time proof authorise an organization relationship indefinitely.

proof.description: payload_digest = sha256(canonical_json(receipt with proof omitted)). detached_jws signs canonical_json({context:'ak.organization_registration_receipt_proof.v1', payload_digest, issuer_id, registration_receipt_id, organization_id, organization_did, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); created_at MUST equal issued_at. Consumers validate the registered organization's organization_did and project it to organization_id, then independently obtain the issuer service's verified resolution, require its service_did to project to issuer_id, and verify verification_method as a signing-time assertionMethod.

OrganizationRegistrationRefreshRequestBo.description: Re-prove control at a newer resolved version and re-issue the receipt. Scopes are not re-negotiated here; a scope change is a new ensure. Refresh exists because a binding pinned to one version stops proving current control the moment the organization rotates its controller.

organization_did.description: Current published Organization DID at the refreshed version. MUST project to organization_id before the refreshed proof is accepted.

OrganizationRegistrationRevokeRequestBod.description: Withdraw the local binding. This is a local act with local effect only: it does not modify, deactivate or annotate the external DID's method history, which this deployment does not control.

reason_code.description: Closed reason set. superseded: replaced by a new binding for the same organization. withdrawn: the deployment or the organization ended the relationship.

OrganizationRegistrationScope.description: Closed set of local administrative scopes a registration may delegate. organization_profile_manage covers this deployment's local organization profile and display; organization_realm_endorse permits issuing ak.realm.organization statements on the organization's behalf; organization_service_delegate permits declaring organization-to-service delegations locally. The set is closed because an open scope vocabulary would let a deployment mint authority the organization never consented to. Holding a scope is a permission to act later, not an action: registration by itself creates no Realm, membership, governance-Station authority, capability or service delegation.

ProjectionAssignedToRelation.description: Read-model edge backing a Strand assigned_to Relation. relation_id is needed by clients to tombstone the assignment; actor_id mirrors the Relation to_ref.

allOf.$comment: common-fields.md 5.3.1: stage_changed_at MUST NOT appear without stage. Tested on the string form because the nullable convention lets both members be present-and-null.

stage.description: Business-progression stage from the domain current result; null or absent when the object has never been written by ak.<kind>.stage.set. Orthogonal to the physical lifecycle in state (common-fields.md 5.3).

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition; MUST NOT be present without stage (common-fields.md 5.3.1).

kind.description: Space kind such as `board`, `list`, `folder`, or a profile-registered kind.

allOf.$comment: common-fields.md 5.3.1: stage_changed_at MUST NOT appear without stage. Tested on the string form because the nullable convention lets both members be present-and-null.

stage.description: Business-progression stage from the domain current result; null or absent when the object has never been written by ak.<kind>.stage.set. Orthogonal to the physical lifecycle in state (common-fields.md 5.3).

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition; MUST NOT be present without stage (common-fields.md 5.3.1).

title.description: Derived display title from plaintext-visible Strand metadata.title; null when metadata is encrypted or hidden from the service profile.

summary.description: Derived display summary from plaintext-visible Strand metadata.summary; null when metadata is encrypted or hidden from the service profile.

board_space_id.description: Derived board Space id from strand_position; not canonical Strand object state.

list_space_id.description: Derived list Space id from strand_position; not canonical Strand object state.

rank.description: Derived rank within list_space_id from strand_position.

assigned_actor_ids.description: Derived current full ActorIds from visible active Relation(relation_kind=assigned_to, from_ref=strand_id), preserving Station identity. Empty or absent means the Strand is unassigned for this projection caller. This is read-model state, not canonical Strand object metadata.

assigned_to_relations.description: Read-only active assigned_to Relation edges backing assigned_actor_ids. Clients use relation_id to tombstone assignments.

is_default.description: DERIVED, not independent storage: true iff strand_id == the parent Realm projection's default_strand_id (the authoritative pointer written by ak.realm.set_default_strand). The projector computes this from Realm.default_strand_id; a stale/dangling pointer never resolves to is_default=true because the reducer rejects set_default_strand against a non-existent Strand. Clients identify the Realm's default discussion Strand deterministically from this flag (or equivalently from Realm.default_strand_id) and MUST NOT infer the default from any Strand-reuses-Realm-token or other implementation detail. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md (default-Strand discovery).

payload_digest.description: Optional digest commitment to the canonical payload object before masking.

inclusion_proof.description: Optional proof that the suite-bearing digest decoded from event_id is included in an Event set or RealmCommit root visible to the caller; it does not prove historical completeness.

reducer_input.description: Redacted views are projection-only evidence and MUST NOT be fed into a reducer as Event Envelope input.

event_id.description: Present only when the source event id is already visible to the caller; omitted when even the event id would distinguish target existence.

realm_id.description: The source Realm boundary visible to the caller. Target Realm identifiers hidden by reference-disclosure policy MUST NOT appear.

reason_code.description: Reasons that would reveal target existence MUST be collapsed to not_found_or_unauthorized for unauthorized callers.

inclusion_proof.description: Optional non-disclosing proof commitment. MUST NOT contain hidden target refs or target Realm metadata.

reducer_input.description: Locked stubs are projection-only evidence and MUST NOT be fed into a reducer as Event Envelope input.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: W3C DID Core 1.0, DID document core properties
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: A raw DID document is emitted and resolved verbatim, so its property names belong to the DID Core lexicon; identity-did.md forbids re-spelling them as snake_case.
A DID document service entry keeps the DID Core lexicon for every member it declares, including the Arkret-defined serviceKind extension property that sits beside serviceEndpoint.
A verification method is resolved and verified verbatim from the DID document, so publicKeyMultibase keeps the DID Core spelling.

did.description: Complete service DID. It MUST equal inception_operation.state.id and the adapter projection MUST equal the resulting service_id.

idempotency_key.description: Bounded opaque caller-chosen correlation string used only to relate audit records for one ensure attempt. It is deliberately outside the ak: typed-ID namespace and MUST NOT be parsed by the typed-ID parser or treated as an object identity. Registration identity is the canonical (service_kind, public_base_url) key that Provider persistence enforces with UNIQUE(service_kind, public_base_url), and the single idempotency authority for this operation is the operation registry's idempotency_mechanism=object_id; this field never establishes a second one.

public_base_url.description: Canonical service base URL: lower-case scheme and host, no query or fragment, normalized path, and exactly one trailing slash. Production deployments MUST use https; explicit development deployments MAY use http.

ServiceRegistrationReceipt.description: Provider-signed stable service-registration receipt. registration_receipt_id is ak:service_registration_receipt:<lowercase hex SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt claims))>. service_id is the projected did_core_id and did is the verified DID. proof is a detached JWS over the ak.service_registration_receipt_proof.v1 binding object; consumers verify the provider through its own resolution evidence.

control_key_digest.description: Digest of the active control/update public key at version_id; this is not the next-key commitment or private recovery material.

proof.description: payload_digest = sha256(canonical_json(receipt with proof omitted)). detached_jws signs canonical_json({context:'ak.service_registration_receipt_proof.v1', payload_digest, provider_id, registration_receipt_id, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); created_at MUST equal issued_at. Consumers resolve the provider did, require project(did)=provider_id, and verify verification_method as a signing-time assertionMethod of that did.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: W3C Verifiable Credential Data Integrity 1.0, proofs
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: The proof is verified byte-for-byte against the external DID log, so every member keeps the Data Integrity spelling.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: did:webvh v1.0, the DID log file
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: A DID log entry must round-trip byte-for-byte with the external log, so versionId and versionTime keep the did:webvh spelling.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: did:webvh v1.0, did:webvh DID method parameters
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: The parameters object is hashed and verified as part of the external DID log entry, so scid, method, updateKeys and nextKeyHashes are mirrored verbatim.

updateKeys.description: Exactly one active service-controlled update key. On a rotation entry it MUST open the previous entry's sole nextKeyHashes commitment; spent keys MUST NOT be reused.

nextKeyHashes.description: Exactly one sha2-256 multihash/Base58BTC commitment to a next update key generated and durably held by the service. Missing or mismatched commitments fail closed as service_prerotation_invalid.

SessionGrantCredentialClass.description: Closed credential class. recovery_session is a <=15 minute, non-refreshable, DPoP-bound candidate-device grant restricted to the exact recovery operation set; recovery completion issues a distinct standard grant.

SessionGrantDeviceBinding.description: Authorization state committed into a standard device grant. An Account Authority MUST populate it verbatim from the allow receipt of ak.peer.device_revocations.command.check.v1, which is the only source of the origin-derived authorization Event and generation; it MUST NOT be taken from client input, a local cache or a private lookup. Stations compare it with the current active device generation on admission.

model_generation_ref.description: PCR-local monotonic generation. It MUST NOT equal or be derived from a DID versionId.

proof_jwt.description: Frozen initial holder proof authenticated by the Agent request digest. HTTP DPoP is fresh per attempt and must bind the same public JWK thumbprint, not necessarily identical JWT bytes. First validation checks both proofs; completed exact ledger replay reuses validated body proof while revalidating fresh HTTP DPoP. See key-management section 3.6.1.

SessionGrantIntrospectGrant.description: Non-secret grant metadata returned to the validating Station. Never includes the grant JWT, refresh token, or session private key.

audience_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the resource service this grant is valid for.

session_public_key.description: Session signing key (JWK) for RFC 9421 PoP verification on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.2). Server-to-server only.

cnf_jkt.description: RFC 7638 JWK SHA-256 thumbprint of the holder (DPoP) key the grant is bound to (cnf.jkt); the Station uses it to verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3). Server-to-server only.

holder_binding.description: Required closed accepted human-device, recovery candidate-device, or Agent-runtime holder binding.

device_binding.description: Exact origin-derived device authorization preimage taken from the revocation gate's allow receipt. Required only for standard human_device grants and forbidden for recovery candidate-device and Agent grants.

active.description: Whether the grant is currently valid for the requested audience. READ-ONLY: introspection never consumes the grant.

proof_required.description: Whether an additional S2S holder proof is required to confirm the grant active for this introspection request. Default Station grant+DPoP validation uses the request DPoP instead of this field.

one_time_use_consumed.description: Always false: introspection is read-only and never consumes single-use state (rotation is the refresh endpoint's job).

SessionGrantIntrospectRequestBody.description: Server-to-server session-grant introspection request. Exactly one of id / grant_jwt identifies the grant.

id.description: Grant id. Mutually exclusive with grant_jwt.

grant_jwt.description: The signed grant JWT to introspect. Mutually exclusive with id.

audience_id.description: Stable service did_core_id the caller is validating the grant for; a mismatch yields status audience_mismatch.

proof.description: Optional S2S holder confirmation signed by the session key bound into the grant. Stations validating /_arkret/self/* grant+DPoP requests do not require a client-carried introspection proof; they verify the request DPoP locally against the returned cnf_jkt.

proof_jwt.description: JWS over ak.session_grant.introspection_proof.v1 claims (session_grant_id, grant_jwt_digest, audience, challenge, issued_at, expires_at).

account_id.description: Exact protocol account bound to this grant. Both components are signed; clients and resource services MUST NOT reconstruct either component from local state.

session_grant.description: Short-lived bearer/session grant bound to the requested principal, device and audience.

session_grant_id.description: Stable id of the issued or rotated session grant. Returned for every grant so the client can reference, refresh, introspect or revoke this exact grant without re-parsing the opaque session_grant.

session_public_key.description: JWK of the holder/session key the grant is bound to (the device holder key). The client needs this to perform RFC 9421 PoP and to derive the DPoP cnf.jkt for /_arkret/self/* requests (api-conventions.md §3.2 / §3.3); returning it avoids a mandatory introspect round-trip before the first self-path request.

audience_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the Station or resource service the grant is valid for. MUST equal the grant's bound audience.

previous_session_grant_id.description: Present only on refresh. The predecessor grant atomically superseded by this successor.

AcceptedDevicePossessionProof.description: Accepted-device Ed25519 possession proof shared by human SessionGrant issue and refresh. The signature covers utf8('ak.session_grant_accepted_device_possession_proof.v1\n') followed by RFC 8785 JCS of this complete object with signature omitted. It is not a server challenge: freshness comes from the <=300 second signed window, the one-time account handoff or predecessor grant, the issuer request identity, and issuer-ledger exact replay. The origin Station MUST verify this proof with the durable current accepted-device key in the same linearization that evaluates current authorization.

account_handoff_grant_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the exact opaque DPoP-bound account_handoff_grant presented in Authorization; the credential itself MUST NOT enter the proof or logs.

account_id.description: Exact account whose accepted device signs this proof. The verification method controller is projected only to account_id.principal_id; the accepted AccountHandoff or predecessor grant independently binds account_id.station_id.

holder_jkt.description: RFC 7638 thumbprint of the DPoP holder key for the handoff or predecessor SessionGrant.

session_intent_digest.description: Digest of the complete canonical immutable issue or refresh intent.

expires_at.description: MUST be after issued_at and no more than 300 seconds later.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the accepted device key; its fragment MUST identify device_id and its bare did MUST project to account_id.principal_id.

signature.description: 64-byte raw Ed25519 signature encoded as canonical unpadded base64url.

AgentSessionRefreshProof.description: Current Agent runtime-key proof for SessionGrant rotation. It is a distinct branch from accepted human-device PoP and carries no client-generated challenge or polymorphic proof_kind.

expires_at.description: MUST be after issued_at and no more than 300 seconds later.

grant_jwt.description: Near-expiry human DPoP-bound SessionGrant presented as Authorization: DPoP plus a matching DPoP proof.

audience_id.description: If present, MUST equal the predecessor grant audience.

grant_jwt.description: Near-expiry Agent DPoP-bound SessionGrant presented as Authorization: DPoP plus a matching DPoP proof.

audience_id.description: If present, MUST equal the predecessor grant audience.

SessionGrantRefreshRequestBody.description: Closed human-versus-Agent SessionGrant rotation union. Neither branch accepts a client-generated challenge or a generic proof_kind enum.

HumanSessionGrantRequest.description: Returning-human issuance from an already bound account. Authorization is the DPoP-bound account_handoff_grant plus matching per-request DPoP; the body deliberately carries neither a second holder signature nor requested_scope.

RecoverySessionGrantRequest.description: Fresh-device existing-principal recovery issuance. Authorization is the Bound AccountHandoff plus matching per-request DPoP. The Account Authority binds this request to its account/principal mapping and does not consume the handoff on success.

agent_key_authorization_ref.description:
`ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. Event ref of the accepted
`ak.agent.key.authorize` that authorized the runtime key. REQUIRED when
`proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; MUST be omitted for human session grants.

agent_scope_request.description:
`ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. Narrowing hints for the
issued session scope. Service-surface requested_scope values are intersected
with the immutable provision requested_scope, accepted agent_key_scope and
endpoint/resource policy; content actions are additionally intersected with
independent effective Realm capability grants, participation, membership,
history visibility and E2EE policy. Provision mandatory constraints remain in
force at every layer. REQUIRED when `proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; MUST
be omitted for human session grants. `track_names` is a request-side narrowing
field only — the materialized session grant MUST express track scope via the
canonical `allowed_tracks` constraint, not via a new `track_names` grant.

requested_scope_disclosure.description: Optional only for the agent_key_proof branch. A runtime includes this controller-signed private disclosure when the Account Authority does not yet hold verifier-private ceiling evidence established by pairing or an authenticated private evidence transfer. If absent, the authority MUST resolve an already verified disclosure keyed by the same agent_id, DID commitment digest, verifier and audience; a service-local Agent row alone is insufficient.

dpop_binding_proof.description: `ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. DPoP proof JWT for the holder key that the issued session grant will bind to. REQUIRED when `proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; the Account Authority verifies the proof and materializes the resulting JWK thumbprint into the issued grant's `cnf.jkt` / session_public_key binding.

applet_authority.description: Applet-specific delegated session binding. When present, the session grant, proof digest, persistence row, introspection metadata, and revoke selector are bound to the same applet_id, effective_scope, and registration_epoch.

challenge.description: Runtime-generated canonical unpadded Base64URL challenge with at least 128 bits of cryptographic randomness. Frozen for exact issuance retry; not a pairing handle or a server-issued challenge.

audience_id.description: Verified target resource service identity; independent of HTTP Host and transport issuer routing.

verification_method.description: `ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. DID URL of the runtime signing key. REQUIRED when `proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; the verifier MUST parse and adapter-validate its canonical bare did component, require project(did)=principal_id, and then validate the referenced key at the accepted method-history position. A did_core_id MUST NOT be used as a DID URL prefix or concatenated with a fragment. Projection mismatch returns `verification_method_principal_mismatch`. MUST be omitted for human proof kinds.

signature.description: Canonical unpadded Base64URL raw Ed25519 signature over RFC 8785 JCS of the entire proof with signature omitted; no Event JWS wrapper or extra prefix.

proof.description: Closed initial Agent proof. Require 0 < expires_at-issued_at <= 300 seconds, issued_at <= now+30 seconds, and now < expires_at for first validation. No additional nonce. Exact completed issuer-ledger replay reuses durable one-shot verification, with fresh matching-holder HTTP DPoP.

SessionGrantRequestBody.description: Closed returning-human, Agent runtime or fresh-device recovery issuance union. OIDC authorization codes are consumed only by account_handoff_request_body and never by this operation.

SignalSubmitOutcome.description: Result of transient Signal admission. accepted=true means the service placed the encrypted envelope on the short-lived rail; it creates no Event, RealmCommit, authority-stream position or durable delivery receipt.

envelope_digest.description: Digest of the admitted complete encrypted envelope, used only for short-lived replay suppression and local correlation.

dispatched_recipient_count.description: Optional implementation hint for fanout recipients queued locally.

status.description: Retained on purpose: DeviceMessagesSendOutcome dispatches this item by its position in the delivered map, and the status member keeps a detached item self-describing against DeviceMessageUnknownRow. It is a positional discriminator, not a success-only outcome constant.

Retained on purpose: DeviceMessagesSendOutcome dispatches this item by its position in the unknown_devices map, and the status member keeps a detached item self-describing against DeviceMessageDeliveredRow. It is a positional discriminator, not a success-only outcome constant.

SignedSessionGrantClaims.description: Canonical signed claims carried by an ak.session.grant JWT. Except for the fixed kind and derived jti, the closed issuance preimage fields are copied from these claims. credential_class and holder_binding are signed and jointly determine the authorization profile; recovery_session is never refreshable or upgradable and recovery completion issues a distinct standard credential. Verifiers MUST RFC 8785-canonicalize the complete claim-derived preimage, recompute SHA-256, prepend the active sha256 suite wire code, derive ak:session_grant:<44-char-token>, and require byte equality with jti. Changing either binding therefore changes the ID.

issuance_nonce.description: Canonical unpadded Base64URL encoding of the issuer-generated 256-bit issuance nonce. Exact replay reuses the same nonce, issuance preimage, grant ID and JWT.

account_id.description: Exact AccountId bound into this signed grant and its derived session_grant_id.

session_public_key.description: A supported public JWK serialized as its exact RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 string. Producers MUST parse and canonicalize input before signing; consumers MUST reject strings whose parsed JWK re-serialization is not byte-identical. Private JWK members are forbidden.

audience_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the resource service. HTTP origins are bound separately by DPoP htu and MUST NOT be used as the SessionGrant audience.

SessionGrantReplayExpiredProblem.description: Closed RFC 9457 Problem Details extension members for session_grant_replay_expired. The named issuer-ledger record remains authoritative and no replacement grant is created under the same request identity.

state.description: Retained on purpose: this is an RFC 9457 Problem Details extension member on the failure path and names the issuer-ledger state that caused the rejection, so the problem document stays self-describing next to SessionGrantReplayTerminalProblem. It is not a success-only outcome constant.

SessionGrantReplayTerminalProblem.description: Closed RFC 9457 Problem Details extension members for session_grant_replay_terminal. The state is an exact durable issuer-ledger terminal state and no replacement grant is created under the same request identity.
